hens_rule_text: Up to 6 chickens (combined with rabbits and hares) may be kept on residential land without a special license; more than 6 requires a license.
permit_notes: No permit needed for up to 6 chickens. To keep more than 6, or any fowl species other than chickens, the owner must get a license under Sec. 90.078, which requires written consent from 100% of owners of real estate within 100 ft of the applicant's property.
setback_notes: A search-result extract of the licensing section cites a 25 ft coop setback from any neighboring dwelling; this could not be confirmed by direct fetch of the full Sec. 90.078 text.
coop_rules: Keeping of animals may not create a nuisance; livestock in general is banned citywide except on AG-zoned land.
zoning_notes: Livestock is banned within city limits except on property zoned AG (Agricultural District); this rule sits alongside, and is broader than, the 6-chicken household allowance.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Sioux Falls, SD Code of Ordinances, Sec. 90.008 Keeping of Animals (via Internet Archive copy of amlegal)
Sioux Falls, SD Code of Ordinances, Sec. 90.078 Licensing of Animals and Fowl

research_notes: Read the full text of Sec. 90.008 via an August 2025 Internet Archive snapshot of the amlegal code page, which directly confirms the 6-chicken cap, rooster ban, and explicit slaughter ban. Sec. 90.078 (license and 100 ft neighbor consent for more than 6 birds, and the 25 ft coop setback figure) comes from a search-result extract only, since that page was not archived; treated as medium-confidence detail within an otherwise high-confidence record.
